title: Escalation-paths-card-based-ux-proposal-wip
summary: Working draft: a card-based editor and visualizer for SLO thresholds + escalation paths. Goal is to reduce config complexity, make policies readable for on-call and product owners, and surface defaults and guardrails for safe rollouts.
content:
Context and goal:

We need a lightweight, discoverable UI for building alerting policies tied to SLOs and routes that non-SRE stakeholders (PMs, product owners, CS) can understand. Current YAML / rule-heavy flows are a barrier during onboarding and cause misconfigured escalation chains that either spam the team or silently drop important signals.

This doc proposes a card-based composer where each policy is a stack of cards: source (SLO or metric), condition (threshold / ratio / derivative), action set (channels + escalation timeline), and guardrails (silencing windows, annotation requirements, auto-mitigations). The same cards double as a read-only 'execution timeline' that shows how an incoming incident will flow.

Design principles:
- Make the path of an alert legible at a glance (who gets pinged, when, what payload).
- Provide sensible defaults that align with our tiered capacity levels (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
- Keep authoring tight: minimal fields for 80% of policies, advanced options tucked behind an "advanced" toggle.
- Surface traceability: link to SLO definitions, runbooks, and linked Jira tickets.

Primary components (card types):
1) Source card:
  - Label: SLO / route name (autocomplete).
  - Scope badge: global / org / customer-id / project.
  - Preview metrics: current error budget burn rate, 30m and 6h windows (sparklines).
  - Link to SLO definition and a quick-run "simulate" button (simulate a breach and show execution preview).

2) Condition card (one or more):
  - Condition type dropdown: threshold (>=, <=), rate (errors/min), ratio (errors/requests), derivative (delta over time), missing-data.
  - Expression builder: human-readable sentence, e.g., "When error rate >= 5% for 3m". Keep inline editing with tokenized chips for values and units.
  - Preview result: sample events that would match (click to expand).

3) Action set card:
  - Channel selector grid: Slack channel(s) / Email group(s) / PagerDuty escalation / Webhook / Console Notification. Channels render as colored chips with icons.
  - Escalation timeline: drag-to-set timeline lanes (0m, 5m, 15m, 30m, 1h, custom). Each lane contains cards for recipients and a short template preview of the message payload.
  - Throttling/aggregation control: group by fingerprint, minimum repeat suppression window.

4) Guardrail & policy card:
  - Auto-fallback: fallback model or route (e.g., route to lower-cost model variant if 2x baseline latency).
  - Quiet hours: schedule blocks or per-timezone rules.
  - Annotation requirement: require a runbook ID or RFC link before 'Notify Pager' is allowed.
  - Auto-remediation hooks: link to playbook runbook (executes webhook to ops-runbook service).

Execution preview mode:
- Toggling preview animates a sample incident and shows cards lighting up in sequence: source -> matched condition -> action lanes firing.
- Each action displays the payload and substitution tokens used (SLO name, current burn rate, top affected route).
- Preview has a 'what-if' slider to alter severity and see different escalation results.

Wireframe notes (quick sketches / layout):
- Left rail: SLO catalog filter (service, team, sla tier).
- Main canvas: vertical stack of cards forming a policy. Cards are collapsible. Top shows a one-line summary (if you collapse all).
- Right rail: execution preview + history (recent policy firings, last 24h).
- Modal for channel config: editing Slack integration shows sample message preview and an opt-in toggle for actionable buttons (ack, runbook link, auto-snooze).

Backlog grooming notes from meeting 2025-09-05:
- Priority stories (MVP):
  1) Card composer + create/save policy (INFER-742). Minimal condition types (threshold, ratio) and channels (Slack, Email, PagerDuty).
  2) Execution preview for single-condition policies (no fancy sim).
  3) Channel modal with message templating and test-send.
- Stretch (next sprint): multi-condition boolean logic (AND/OR), automatic suggestions for thresholds based on historical percentile, throttling UI.
- Nice-to-have: multi-tenant default templates for customers using Dedicated/Private with specific compliance constraints (require 2 approvers for PagerDuty).

Edge cases / open questions:
- How do we represent merged incidents that match multiple policies? Proposed: execution preview shows dedupe-ranking (policy priority + first-wins), and on real execution we route to a single canonical incident with merged timeline. Need input from SRE on dedupe algorithm. (Action: @Tom to sync with SRE team, ticket: INFER-768)
- Authorization model: who can edit escalation timelines? We need role controls (owner, editor, viewer) — align with existing console RBAC. Add a small lock icon on the top-right of the policy card.
- Rate-limits + billing: policies that send >1000 notifications/day should surface cost warning; link to Optimize suggestions.

Content for product messaging / help text (for UI):
- "Escalation timeline" tooltip: "Define who gets notified and when. Use lanes to add delays. Cards in each lane will be triggered when the condition remains true at that delay."
- "Simulate" tooltip: "Run a pretend incident based on historical data to preview how this policy fires. No external channels will be contacted."

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- User can author a new policy using cards, select an SLO, add one condition, pick up to three channels, and save.
- Execution preview shows the sequence without sending real messages.
- Channel test-send works for Slack and Email.
- Stored policies render in a readable one-line summary in the policies list.

Implementation notes for engineering handoff:
- Backend model: keep policy as list-of-cards (flat schema) that maps to existing alert-rule DSL. Add a small compatibility layer to convert to/from existing YAML.
- UI: React + component library tokens. Card components should be small and composable. Animation in preview should be purely client-side.
- Metrics to capture: policy_create, policy_edit, policy_preview_run, policy_test_send, policy_fire_count. Add tags for escalation path length.

To-dos before next review (owner: Aisha):
- Finalize the default timeline buckets and suppression defaults (action: consult SRE, due 2025-09-12).
- Produce a 3-slide demo for leadership showing the preview animation and one saved policy (Tom + Jia, due 2025-09-14).
- Split engineering tickets: UI components, backend compatibility layer, execution preview backend stub (Riley to create tickets).

Notes from quick user interview (internal beta testers):
- PMs liked card metaphors; ask for a "compact mode" where they can scan 20 policies quickly.
- On-call engineers want stronger dedupe controls and ability to pin a policy to 'suppress duplicates for team'.
- CS wants ability to attach a customer-facing message to notifications for high-profile customers (Dedicated customers).

Appendix: example policy (natural language):
- When SLO "Embed API latency" 95th percentile > 1.2s for 10m, notify #embeddings-oncall on Slack immediately, notify #platform-engineering-email after 15m, escalate to PagerDuty with high urgency at 30m if still failing. Suppress repeats for 60m. During quiet hours (00:00-06:00 PST) only escalate to PagerDuty if severity is "critical".

References / links (quick):
- Jira: INFER-742 (composer MVP), INFER-768 (dedupe), INFER-755 (channel modal).
- Confluence: /console/alerts/escalation-patterns (draft runbooks).
- Slack thread: #console-design pinned message 2025-08-28 (notes).

Draft sign-off:
- Product: Aisha Patel (owner)
- UX: Jia Wen (review)
- Eng: Riley O'Connor (feasibility)
- SRE: Tom Schaefer (policy semantics)

Open: schedule follow-up review 2025-09-15 to lock MVP scope.
